subject: Renewal: Dedicated Capacity amendment — request to expand 16→32 GPUs
participants_external: anna.lee@vectorhealth.com (Anna Lee, Head of ML Ops)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lee <anna.lee@vectorhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + optional capacity expansion (16→32 GPUs) — draft amendment attached

Hi Anna —

Hope you had a good week. VectorHealth's renewal for the Dedicated pool is coming up on Mar 1 and I wanted to surface an option that I think aligns with your Q2 performance goals. Based on the usage patterns we reviewed last quarter, your 16-GPU reserved pool is frequently saturating during peak windows.

Two optional paths we can do as part of the renewal:
- Keep current 16 GPUs and extend term (12/24 months) — standard renewal
- Expand to 32 GPUs reserved (same cluster, dedicated pool) with revised per-hour reserved pricing and an SLA for steady-state throughput —Recommended if you need predictable peak throughput for model X inference.

I've attached a draft amendment and a pricing proposal (RH_Pricing_Proposal_32gpu.xlsx) illustrating the per-GPU reserved hourly and total monthly commit. Quick note on timing: if you confirm the expansion before Mar 1 we can provision the extra nodes during the renewal processing window and avoid any temporary capacity delays.

Attached: VectorHealth_Renewal_Amendment_v2.pdf (amendment draft), RH_Pricing_Proposal_32gpu.xlsx (pricing scenarios).

Would you be available for a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk through the SLA and pricing options?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Anna Lee <anna.lee@vectorhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:03:21 -0500
Subject: Re: Renewal + optional capacity expansion (16→32 GPUs) — draft amendment attached

Karthik —

Thanks for the heads-up and the materials. We appreciate you flagging the saturation. A few clarifying questions before we lock anything in: 

1) Throughput guarantee: what does the SLA look like for the 32-GPU pool? We need a clear measurable (p99 token latency or sustained tokens/sec per GPU) tied to remediation.
2) Pricing: last year we committed to 16 GPUs at $2.75/hr per GPU reserved. Can you outline the blended per-GPU reserved rate for 32 GPUs? Our procurement team is pushing for no more than a 10% increase in total monthly commit vs. current spend.
3) Provisioning timeline: if we sign on Mar 1, how soon will the additional GPUs be available for production? We run training and inference workflows that cannot tolerate long delays.

If it's easier, happy to take a quick call tomorrow afternoon.

- Anna
Anna Lee
Head of ML Ops | VectorHealth
anna.lee@vectorhealth.com

Subject: Fwd: Renewal + optional capacity expansion (VectorHealth) — pricing/SLA ask

Team — looping you in on VectorHealth's questions below. Key asks: SLA metric details and a blended per-GPU reserved rate that keeps their total monthly commit within ~10% of current spend if possible. They currently have 16 GPUs at $2.75/hr/GPU reserved. They want to double to 32 GPUs.

Options I think we can offer quickly:
- 12-month term, 32 GPUs, $2.25/hr per-GPU reserved (volume discount) — provisioning within 7 business days after signature, SLA: 95th percentile latency target for their standard 2k-token requests and a throughput target of X tokens/sec per GPU (we need Rishi to confirm numbers).
- 24-month term, 32 GPUs, $1.95/hr per-GPU reserved — deeper discount with a longer commit; provisioning same window.

Rishi — can you confirm whether the throughput guarantee and remediation ladder below are acceptable operationally? If yes, I'll send both formal options to VectorHealth.

----- Forwarded message -----
"""
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:10:13 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal + optional capacity expansion (VectorHealth) — pricing/SLA ask

Karthik —

We can support the two-tier pricing you outlined. A couple operational clarifications: 

- Throughput guarantee: propose we commit to 95th percentile inference latency <= 350ms for their 2k-token baseline request profile and steady-state throughput of >= 45 tokens/sec per GPU for their model on A100s (quoted per our profiling).
- Remediation: if SLA breach occurs for two consecutive weeks we provide pro-rated credits for affected hours and priority remediation with a 4-hour on-call response.
- Provisioning: If procurement sign-off occurs during the renewal window, we can provision extra instances within 5 business days (we'll reserve the nodes in the region).

From a cost standpoint the $2.25/hr for 12 months and $1.95/hr for 24 months are fine — we can mark those as reserved per-GPU-hour.

Marissa/Sean — does that pricing need a commercial approval or legal redlines?

Rishi
Senior PM, Inference Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 07:33:00 -0800
Subject: Revised renewal options — VectorHealth (16→32 GPUs)

Anna —

Thanks for the questions and for looping procurement in. Based on our internal ops review here are two formal options you can choose from: 

Option A — 12-month term (recommended for ramp flexibility)
- Reserved capacity: 32 GPUs (same physical cluster)
- Per-GPU reserved rate: $2.25/hr
- SLA: 95th percentile inference latency <= 350ms on VectorHealth's 2k-token baseline; steady-state throughput >= 45 tokens/sec per GPU
- Remediation: pro-rated credits for affected hours after two consecutive SLA breach weeks; 4-hour on-call priority remediation
- Provisioning: additional GPUs available within 5 business days after countersignature

Estimated financials (monthly): current spend (16 GPUs @ $2.75/hr) ~ $95k/month (example). Option A expected monthly commit for 32 GPUs @ $2.25/hr ~ $123k/month (approx +29% raw compute) — note: we can apply a one-time onboarding credit to reduce first invoice if helpful.

Option B — 24-month term (deeper discount)
- Reserved capacity: 32 GPUs
- Per-GPU reserved rate: $1.95/hr
- Same SLA and remediation terms as Option A
- Provisioning window: 5 business days post-signature

Estimated financials (monthly): 32 GPUs @ $1.95/hr ~ $106.7k/month (approx +12% vs current) — this is the plan that hits your procurement request of ~10% budget delta (with rounding and factoring in usage patterns).

Next steps: If Option B works for you, we can push an amendment and DocuSign link and I can ask finance to prepare the 24-month payment schedule. If you'd prefer Option A, we can provision faster and include a one-time onboarding credit.

Attached: VectorHealth_Renewal_Amendment_v2.pdf, RH_Pricing_Proposal_32gpu.xlsx

Open to a quick call to finalize.

Thanks,
Karthik
